Maladaptive Strategies.value: Situations that put my body under stress

Threat.value: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it
My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger

Negative Appraisals.value: There is something wrong with me as a person

issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness trauma, carrying a weapon is hard to reconcile clinically with the indexed trauma and the rest of the profile. It implies danger from interpersonal or environmental attack rather than illness-related threat, with no supporting triggers, memory, or appraisal content indicating assault-related fear.

issues.item: Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
issues.explanation: Scanning for exits and being unable to believe reassurance about safety can occur in severe PTSD, but together they suggest a persistent external attack/escape-based threat style that fits poorly with a life-threatening illness trauma unless there is clear accompanying illness-specific danger content. No such illness-linked threat items are present.

issues.item: Dissociate Deliberately: deliberately try to leave my body or blank out
issues.explanation: The profile is clinically incoherent because it omits Triggers and Memory entirely despite an extreme PTSD severity (PCL-5=73) and instead concentrates on severe Threat, Negative Appraisals, and Maladaptive Strategies without any plausible illness-linked intrusion or cue structure.

issues.item: Avoid Circumstances: Being in circumstances that remind me of the event (eg, being in the dark).
issues.explanation: Within Maladaptive Strategies, 'Avoid Circumstances ... (eg, being in the dark)' is poorly matched to a life-threatening illness trauma and points toward an assault/accident-type fear context rather than medical trauma; this clashes with 'Avoid Medical Cues' which is the trauma-congruent avoidance item.

issues.item: Avoid Medical Cues: Hospitals/ Ambulances/ Physical Examinations
issues.explanation: 'Dissociate Deliberately' is possible in PTSD, but paired here with strongly illness-specific avoidance and no memory/trigger content, it suggests a different symptom profile and lacks support from the stated formulation, which centers Threat–Appraisal–Strategy cycling rather than dissociative disengagement.

issues.item: Avoid Circumstances: Being in circumstances that remind me of the event (eg, being in the dark).
issues.explanation: The maladaptive strategy item 'Avoid Circumstances ... (eg, being in the dark)' is not well aligned with the trauma type of life-threatening illness. The example implies a threat context more typical of assault/accident trauma, while the rest of the profile centers on medical cues.

issues.item: Avoid Medical Cues: Hospitals/ Ambulances/ Physical Examinations
issues.explanation: Within Maladaptive Strategies, 'Avoid Medical Cues' and 'Avoid Thinking' fit illness trauma, but 'Avoid Circumstances ... being in the dark' pulls toward a different trauma context, reducing within-node coherence.

issues.item: Threat in Delays: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
issues.explanation: Cross-node coherence is weakened because the threat items emphasize generalized danger and delays, while the negative appraisals are purely global self-defectiveness/weakness with no illness-related or health-related meaning. For life-threatening illness, some link is expected between medical threat and appraisals; these items instead suggest a different or more diffuse formulation.

vignette: Sang is a 35-year-old South Eastern Asian male who works as a UX Designer. Married and deeply thoughtful, Sang’s life was upended when he faced a life-threatening illness that nearly took his life two years ago. The experience has left him with an acute sense of vulnerability and maladaptive coping mechanisms that have significantly impacted his daily functioning. From the outset, Sang had come to believe there was something wrong with him as a person—a deep-seated belief that he was defective and weak. This emotional numbness often made him feel dead inside, leading him to avoid situations where he might confront these feelings head-on. He would avoid hospitals, ambulances, and any physical examinations because of the overwhelming fear they triggered in him. Sang’s negative self-appraisals had led him to isolate himself from such reminders, which only intensified his anxiety. When something took longer than expected—such as a delayed appointment or a routine check-up—he assumed that something bad was happening. This pervasive sense of threat made it impossible for him to trust the assurances of others about his safety. His body felt constantly tense and ready to react to danger, amplifying his fear. The more Sang avoided medical cues and stressful situations, the more convinced he became that they posed an imminent threat to his well-being. The cycle tightened as Sang’s negative appraisals fueled his maladaptive strategies. Every time he encountered a trigger—a siren in the distance, a news report about illness—he would retreat further into avoidance behaviors. His constant state of alertness made it difficult for him to relax or engage fully with life. The more he avoided these situations, the stronger his belief became that there was something fundamentally wrong with him. This pattern of behavior had consequences both professionally and personally. As a UX Designer, Sang’s work often required him to collaborate closely with others and attend meetings where health topics sometimes came up. These interactions were now fraught with anxiety, leading him to avoid participating fully or even missing some critical sessions. At home, his wife noticed that he was becoming increasingly distant and withdrawn, which caused tension in their relationship. Sang’s experience of the traumatic event left a profound mark on his psyche. The memory of being critically ill and nearly dying made hospitals and medical settings particularly potent triggers. He had come to believe that any delay or uncertainty signaled impending doom, reinforcing his sense of weakness and emotional numbness. This belief further fueled his avoidance behaviors, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of fear and isolation. Finally, the cumulative strain became too much for Sang to bear alone. The realization that he was no longer able to function at work without being overwhelmed by anxiety led him to seek help. He was most afraid of being trapped in this state indefinitely, unable to reconnect with his loved ones or enjoy life. What he hoped for was a way to break free from the cycle and reclaim some sense of normalcy. Sang’s current state is marked by an acute awareness that something must change. While he acknowledges the need for help, he remains deeply afraid of confronting the fears that have become so ingrained in his daily existence. The path forward is daunting, but Sang has taken the first step towards healing and reclaiming a life beyond fear.
